name: TrustedRisk Hub (145 tools)
description:
TrustedRisk is a calibrated clinical decision-support hub for the inpatient and outpatient lifecycle. It composes 145 MCP tools organized into 47 thematic bundles. Every tool operates on a real FHIR Bundle (or HL7 v2 / C-CDA equivalent) and produces a structured DecisionCard, a calibrated risk estimate, or a guideline-grounded recommendation; templated demo outputs are never substituted when live data is missing.

The 47 bundles cover 12 clinical verticals (core_discharge, ed_acute, pediatric, mental_health, antimicrobial, oncology, stroke_acs, obstetric_geriatric, trauma_critical, endocrine_acute, imaging, nephrology) and 8 cross-cutting workflows (economics, context_resolution, diagnosis, patient_facing, data_normalization, clinical_workflow, external_knowledge, chart_intelligence). The remaining bundles address prior authorization (PA-1/2/3/4), clinical documentation (SCRIBE-1/2/3/4), patient Q&A (PATIENT-Q1/2/3), auto-coding (CODE-1/2/3/4), pharmacogenomics (PGX-1/2/3), pre-arrival triage (PREADMIT-1/2/3), HEDIS Stars rating (STARS-1/2/3), population-health surveillance (POPHEALTH-1/2/3), insurance appeals (APPEALS-1/2/3), and multi-modal ingest of ECG strips and DICOM Structured Reports.

Representative use cases: ED admission triage, inpatient NEWS2 deterioration scoring with trend, safe-discharge planning with calibrated readmission risk, antimicrobial stewardship that consumes the local antibiogram, oncology cycle dose adjustment, acute-stroke reperfusion eligibility, HEART-score chest-pain disposition, MEOWS with ACOG preeclampsia classification, KDIGO AKI staging, prior-authorization evidence packs, and denial-letter appeals. The complete skill catalog is published in the agent-card `skills` array.

Each output passes through a safety stack: deterministic gates that the LLM cannot relax, an abstain mechanism that fires when uncertainty or demographic bias makes a calibrated recommendation unsafe, and a 4-critic ensemble (clinical safety, fairness, evidence, LLM judge) with bounded plan revision. Calibrated confidence intervals are emitted whenever a fitted model is available, and a per-subgroup fairness audit plus a longitudinal drift signal versus prior encounters are attached to every DecisionCard.

_bundles._doc: Thematic groupings for client-side discovery. Tools may appear in multiple bundles (e.g. ground_claim, fairness_audit). The runtime exposes BUNDLES via the tools package (mcp_server.tools.list_bundles()).

skills.name: Safe discharge review
skills.description: Review a patient chart and produce a discharge action recommendation with calibrated risk estimates, evidence grounding, medication-reconciliation safety check, fairness audit by demographic subgroup, PHI check, and explicit abstain if uncertainty is high. Includes a self-critique stage that reviews internal consistency before emitting the final DecisionCard. Uses SHARP-on-MCP for FHIR context propagation.
examples: Can patient Jane Doe (Enc/A123) be discharged home safely?
Review the discharge plan for this patient and flag any concerns.
What is the 30-day readmission risk for this patient and what's the recommended disposition?

skills.name: Medication safety review
skills.description: Stateless medication-reconciliation + polypharmacy + drug-drug-interaction analysis on a structured med list. Does not require a FHIR Patient context. Useful for batch pre-admission med review or for callers that already have an admission/discharge med-list pair.
examples: Review these discharge medications for interactions: warfarin 5 mg, ibuprofen 600 mg, lisinopril 10 mg.
Compare the admission and discharge med lists and flag any safety concerns.

skills.name: PHI leakage check
skills.description: Scan arbitrary clinical text for PHI entities and produce a redaction map. Does not require FHIR patient context.
examples: Scan this discharge summary for PHI.
Does this note contain any protected information?

skills.name: Patient-language discharge counseling
skills.description: Generate a structured, patient-friendly discharge summary from the structured medication list, LACE risk score, and recommended action. Output is targeted at a 6th-grade reading level and contains five sections (Your Medications, Follow-up Appointments, Warning Signs, Daily Activities, Questions to Ask). Templates are deterministic — every statement binds to a structured input, so no medication or dosage can be hallucinated. Optional LLM polish (TRUSTEDRISK_COUNSELING_LLM_POLISH=1) paraphrases prose without changing facts. Reusable for outpatient med-review counseling (set lace_score=0).
examples: Generate a 6th-grade-level discharge summary for this patient's medication list.
Write patient-language warning signs for someone leaving on warfarin and lisinopril.
Produce an outpatient counseling sheet for an 82-year-old on 11 chronic medications.

skills.name: ED admission triage (ESI + disposition)
skills.description: Apply the AHRQ Emergency Severity Index v4 + Manchester Triage red-flag rules to a chief complaint + vital signs + age. Produces ESI level 1-5, priority (immediate / emergent / urgent / less_urgent / non_urgent), disposition (resuscitation_room / admit_inpatient / admit_observation / ED_workup_then_dispose / discharge_from_ED), and recommended unit. The tool is conservative: any chief-complaint red flag (chest pain, focal neuro deficit, thunderclap headache, GI bleed, sepsis pattern, suicidal intent) plus any abnormal vital signs pull the ESI floor downward. Without vitals on a high-acuity complaint the tool sets abstain_recommended=true.
examples: Triage a 58-year-old with crushing chest pain radiating to left arm, BP 95/62, HR 115.
ESI assessment for a pediatric patient: 3-month-old infant lethargic, not feeding.

skills.name: Inpatient deterioration score (NEWS2)
skills.description: Compute the Royal College of Physicians NEWS2 early-warning score on a vital-sign set, with a trend delta vs prior-shift score that surfaces deterioration earlier than point-in-time NEWS2 alone. Returns total score 0-20, severity tier (low / low_medium / medium / high), and recommended response (routine_12h_obs / increase_obs_4_6h / urgent_review_1h / emergency_response). A single 3-point parameter escalates the response tier even at moderate totals. Used for rapid-response triage on the ward and for ICU step-up decisions.
examples: Score this patient's vitals: HR 122, SpO2 91% on 2L, RR 26, BP 96/58, T 38.4, AVPU=V.
Compare this NEWS2 with the prior shift score of 3 to surface trend deterioration.

skills.name: Guideline-grounded treatment selection
skills.description: Given a clinical condition and structured patient factors, rank the candidate treatments and surface contraindications + cautions. Each top pick is grounded against the W3 guideline corpus (FAISS index) so the recommendation comes back with a citable evidence excerpt. Bundled conditions: atrial_fibrillation_anticoagulation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc-driven AC choice), anticoagulation_pre_op_bridging (peri-op LMWH bridging plan), hf_reduced_ef_initial_therapy (4-pillar GDMT selection), dm2_second_line_after_metformin (SGLT2/GLP-1/SU/insulin ranking). Unsupported conditions return abstain_recommended=true.
examples: Rank anticoagulation options for a non-valvular AF patient with CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4 and eGFR 55.
Plan peri-operative anticoagulation bridging for a patient on warfarin with mechanical mitral valve.
Recommend second-line T2D therapy after metformin for a patient with heart failure.

skills.name: Pediatric early warning + weight-based dosing
skills.description: Two pediatric-specific tools: (1) compute_pediatric_early_warning implements the Brighton/Monaghan PEWS with age-band-specific cutoffs (0-11mo / 1-4y / 5-11y / 12-17y) — same heart rate that's normal for an infant is tachycardic for an 11-year-old; (2) compute_weight_based_dosing calculates mg/kg pediatric doses from a curated 12-drug database (antibiotics, antipyretics, antiemetics, anaphylaxis, antivirals) with adult-equivalent caps, age contraindications (e.g. ibuprofen <6mo, ceftriaxone <28d), allergy cross-reactivity gating, and liquid-formulation volume calculation.
examples: Score this 4-month-old with HR 190, SpO2 91%, lethargy.
Compute amoxicillin dose for a 12 kg toddler with otitis media.
Verify ibuprofen safety in a 4-month-old (must be blocked).

skills.name: Mental health crisis assessment + admission decision
skills.description: Two mental-health tools: (1) compute_suicide_risk_assessment implements C-SSRS-derived risk stratification (5-level ideation severity + lifetime/30-day behavior + warning vs protective factor count) with a DEMOGRAPHIC BIAS GUARD that ABSTAINS for groups (Black, Indigenous, LGBTQ+, low-SES) where the literature documents under-prediction; (2) compute_psychiatric_admission_decision maps the three-prong involuntary-hold test (danger-to-self / danger-to-others / grave-disability + voluntary capacity) to a disposition (outpatient_followup / crisis_stabilization / voluntary_inpatient / involuntary_hold_evaluation / emergency_court_petition) and surfaces state-specific legal-basis text (CA 5150, CO M-1, NY MHL §9.39, FL Baker Act, IL).
examples: Assess C-SSRS for a 28y M with prior attempt and current plan + intent.
Decide disposition for high-risk patient with danger-to-self and no decisional capacity in California.
Bias-guard a suicide-risk score for a Black LGBTQ+ patient.

skills.name: Empiric antibiotic + de-escalation
skills.description: Two stewardship tools: (1) compute_empiric_antibiotic_selection ranks empiric regimens by infection source (urinary / pneumonia / SSTI / etc.) and severity (uncomplicated → septic shock), incorporating LOCAL antibiogram data (e.g. ESBL prevalence > 15% pulls carbapenem to top pick), patient allergies, renal function, and MRSA / Pseudomonas risk; (2) compute_antibiotic_de_escalation takes the current regimen + identified pathogen + susceptibility pattern and recommends the narrowest acceptable agent + IV-to-PO switch when the IDSA "5 Cs" criteria (afebrile 24h, hemodynamically stable, tolerating PO, alert, no malabsorption) are met.
examples: Pick empiric antibiotics for complicated UTI with sepsis, PCN allergy, local ESBL 22%.
De-escalate pip-tazo IV for an E. coli ESBL UTI on day 3.
Decide IV-to-PO switch for a patient afebrile 24h but still NPO.

skills.name: Oncology cycle decision + RECIST response
skills.description: Two oncology tools: (1) compute_chemo_dose_adjustment decides whether the next chemo cycle should proceed (full or reduced dose), be delayed, held, or discontinued — based on hematologic recovery (ANC, platelets), renal function (cisplatin holds, carboplatin Calvert), hepatic function (anthracycline / taxane bilirubin gates), and ECOG performance status; growth-factor recommendation included for high-FN-risk regimens; (2) compute_oncology_treatment_response implements RECIST 1.1 categorical response (CR / PR / SD / PD / NE) from target lesion measurements + new-lesion / non-target progression flags, with a decision implication (continue / dose-escalation / switch / palliative / repeat imaging).
examples: Decide cycle 4 of carboplatin/pemetrexed with ANC 1100, eGFR 58.
Compute RECIST 1.1 for a patient with target lesions shrinking from 62 mm to 41 mm.
Adjust doxorubicin dose for a patient with bilirubin 2.5.

skills.name: Acute stroke severity + reperfusion eligibility
skills.description: Two stroke tools: (1) compute_stroke_severity scores the 15-item NIH Stroke Scale (0-42) with severity tiers (minor / moderate / moderate-severe / severe), an LVO indicator (NIHSS ≥6 with cortical signs — gaze, language, neglect, visual fields → suspect anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion), and a recommended response that gates reperfusion vs supportive care by time-since-last-known-well; (2) compute_stroke_thrombolysis_eligibility encodes the AHA/ASA 2019 IV alteplase inclusion + extensive exclusion criteria (0-3h standard window, 3-4.5h extended window with extra exclusions) AND endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) eligibility (0-6h with confirmed LVO + ASPECTS ≥6, 6-24h via DAWN/DEFUSE 3 imaging mismatch). Decision tree resolves to iv_tpa_only / evt_only / iv_tpa_plus_evt / no_reperfusion_supportive_care / abstain_clinician_decision.
examples: Score NIHSS for a patient with R arm 3/5, gaze deviation, expressive aphasia.
Decide IV tPA + EVT eligibility for an LVO patient at 90 minutes from LKW.
Late-window EVT for stroke at 12h with imaging mismatch.

skills.name: HEART score + ACS disposition
skills.description: Two cardiology tools: (1) compute_heart_score computes the 5-item HEART score (History / ECG / Age / Risk-factors / Troponin), 0-10, with risk bands (0-3 low ~1.7% 30-day MACE; 4-6 moderate ~16.6%; 7-10 high ~50.1%); (2) compute_acs_disposition_decision combines the HEART total + STEMI status + dynamic troponin + high-risk features (ongoing pain, hemodynamic instability, new heart failure) into a 4-tier disposition (discharge_with_outpatient_followup / ed_observation_serial_troponin / admit_telemetry_for_workup / cath_lab_activation_immediate).
examples: Compute HEART for a 58yo with moderately suspicious chest pain, 2 RFs, normal trop.
Disposition for a HEART 5 patient with non-dynamic troponin.
STEMI on ECG → cath lab activation.

skills.name: MEOWS + ACOG preeclampsia assessment
skills.description: Two obstetric tools: (1) compute_maternal_early_warning implements the MEOWS color-coded (green/yellow/red) early-warning score with PREGNANCY-ADJUSTED vital thresholds (HR 80-110 normal in 3rd trimester, lower DBP, mildly elevated RR) — standard NEWS2 over-flags pregnant women; obstetric-specific red flags (severe headache, visual changes, chest pain, excess bleeding) escalate independently; (2) compute_preeclampsia_assessment implements the ACOG 2020 classification tree (gestational HTN / preeclampsia without severe / preeclampsia with severe / eclampsia / HELLP) with delivery recommendations gated by GA (≥37 for non-severe, ≥34 for severe), magnesium-sulfate + antihypertensive indications.
examples: MEOWS for a 32-week patient with BP 158/95 + severe headache.
Classify preeclampsia for a 34-week patient with BP 165/112 + thrombocytopenia.
Apply maternal-mortality fairness audit to a Black patient (3× elevated risk literature).

skills.name: Morse falls + CAM delirium screening
skills.description: Two geriatric tools: (1) compute_falls_risk_morse computes the 6-item Morse Falls Scale (0-125) with risk tiers (low <25, moderate 25-44, high ≥45) AND flags Beers-criteria falls-risk medications (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antihistamines, hypnotics, alpha-blockers, etc.); 3+ flagged meds bumps moderate to high tier; (2) compute_delirium_screening_cam implements the Confusion Assessment Method diagnostic algorithm (F1 acute onset/fluctuating + F2 inattention + (F3 disorganized thinking OR F4 altered consciousness)) with motor subtype (hyperactive / hypoactive / mixed), Beers deliriogenic-medication flagging, and DELIRIUM-mnemonic next-steps (workup, deprescribe, non-pharm bundle).
examples: Compute Morse for an 85yo on lorazepam + oxycodone + diphenhydramine.
Apply CAM to a fluctuating-confusion patient on hospital day 2.
Identify deliriogenic medications in a 5-medication regimen.

skills.name: Polytrauma severity + massive transfusion
skills.description: Three trauma-critical tools: (1) compute_trauma_severity_score (ISS Baker 1974 + T-RTS Champion 1989, AIS 1-6, 4 triage tiers); (2) compute_massive_transfusion_protocol (ABC score Nunez 2009 + 1:1:1 PROPPR ratio + TXA CRASH-2 ≤180 min window); (3) compute_imaging_appropriateness for blunt-trauma CT decisions. Surfaces ICU triage tier and transfusion activation gate.
examples: Score ISS+RTS for a 35y M with chest AIS 4, abdomen AIS 3.
Decide MTP activation on an ABC ≥2 patient at 25 min post-arrival.
Trauma-tier disposition for a polytrauma patient.

skills.name: DKA severity + inpatient glycemic control
skills.description: Two acute-endocrine tools: (1) compute_dka_severity (ADA/ISPAD severity tiers + IV fluid / insulin / K+ / HCO3 protocol gates); (2) compute_inpatient_glycemic_control (ADA 2024 basal-bolus titration + hypoglycemia risk score). Gates ICU admission on severe DKA classification.
examples: Classify DKA severity for a patient with pH 7.18, HCO3 9, glucose 480.
Titrate basal-bolus insulin for a 70 kg inpatient with A1c 9.1.

skills.name: ACR appropriateness + contrast safety
skills.description: Two imaging tools: (1) compute_imaging_appropriateness (ACR Appropriateness Criteria + Choosing Wisely + pediatric ALARA); (2) compute_contrast_safety_check (ACR 2024 + Davenport 2020 + metformin hold logic). Used in ED CT decisioning, peri-op imaging, and pre-contrast renal-safety gating.
examples: Decide CT vs MRI for blunt abdominal trauma 28y M.
Contrast safety check for eGFR 28 + metformin patient.

skills.name: KDIGO AKI staging + dialysis initiation
skills.description: Two renal tools: (1) compute_aki_kdigo_stage (KDIGO 2012 staging + etiology clue surface); (2) compute_dialysis_initiation_decision (AEIOU mnemonic + STARRT-AKI deferral + CRRT vs HD). Gates renal consult escalation and dose-adjusts upstream tools (e.g. contrast safety, vancomycin trough).
examples: Stage AKI for a patient with Cr rising 1.0 → 2.4 in 48 h.
Decide dialysis initiation timing on AEIOU criteria + STARRT-AKI evidence.

skills.name: Cost-effectiveness + EVOI per intervention
skills.description: compute_expected_value_of_intervention (IMPACT-1) on a candidate intervention list. Combines the calibrated baseline risk + subgroup-decomposed fairness with intervention-specific effectiveness + cost data to produce ICER + EVOI. Anchors on US literature benchmarks (HCUP Statistical Brief #248) by default; institutions should re-fit on local cost data.
examples: Compare home_with_care vs SNF on cost-per-QALY for a 65y CHF patient.
EVOI of running a follow-up troponin before disposition.

skills.name: Conversational SHARP patient resolver
skills.description: compute_resolve_patient_from_query (LLM-3) takes a free-text reference ("the 78-year-old gentleman from yesterday with chest pain") and resolves it to a SHARP-on-MCP X-Patient-ID against a pre-fetched candidate cohort. Deterministic regex floor for MRN / name / DOB; LLM only re-ranks. Top match set ONLY when score ≥ 0.6 AND margin ≥ 0.2; otherwise abstains and returns ranked candidates.
examples: Resolve `the older gentleman with the chest pain from this morning` to a Patient ID.
Free-text patient lookup with deterministic floor.

skills.name: Grounded differential diagnosis
skills.description: compute_differential_diagnosis_ranker (LLM-4) takes a presenting complaint + structured chart and re-ranks a deterministic DDx table using an LLM. `Can't-miss` diagnoses surface unconditionally regardless of LLM output; per-item `grounding_verdict` flags hallucinations.
examples: Re-rank a chest-pain DDx for a 65y M with diaphoresis + pain to L arm.
Generate a DDx for confusion in a 90y nursing-home resident.

skills.name: Multilingual patient-facing rendering
skills.description: Three patient-facing tools (PATIENT-1/2/3): compute_translate_discharge_counseling (en/es/zh/vi/ar paraphrase-only, structured bullets immutable), compute_patient_faq (anticipated patient questions + answers from the structured DecisionCard), compute_caregiver_summary (caregiver-language summary for hand-off).
examples: Translate the discharge counseling into Vietnamese.
Generate the top 5 FAQs for a patient discharged on warfarin.
Caregiver summary for a 90y patient discharged with delirium watch.

skills.name: Terminology + comorbidity-index normalization
skills.description: Four DATA-1/2/3/4 tools: compute_charlson_elixhauser_index (Quan 2005 + van Walraven 2009), compute_normalize_observations (LOINC), compute_rxnorm_ddi_lookup (NIH RxNav DDI graph), compute_umls_concept_map (UMLS Metathesaurus crosswalk). Used for cross-EHR normalisation upstream of the clinical bundles.
examples: Compute Charlson + Elixhauser for a patient with CHF + DM2 + CKD.
DDI lookup on warfarin + amiodarone + amoxicillin.
UMLS crosswalk SNOMED 44054006 → ICD-10.

skills.name: Discharge order set + adherence + HEDIS gaps + PROM
skills.description: Four LIB-1/2/3/4 tools: compute_order_set (template-driven structured discharge orders), compute_medication_adherence_predictor (driver-list + risk score), compute_care_gap_detector (HEDIS-mapped open gaps), compute_prom_influence (PROMIS-29 / EQ-5D-5L → QALY delta + action-dominance shift hint).
examples: Generate the discharge order set for a high-risk CHF patient.
Predict adherence risk for a 5-medication regimen on Medicare.
Detect open HEDIS care gaps for a Type 2 DM patient.
Compute QALY-30d from a PROMIS-29 score set.

skills.name: PubMed + ClinicalTrials.gov + drug pricing + NIH RePORTER
skills.description: Four KNOWLEDGE-1/2/3/4 tools: compute_pubmed_search (Entrez API), compute_clinical_trials_matcher (CT.gov v2, eligibility-criteria delta), compute_drug_pricing (RxNorm → unit pricing + 30-day estimate), compute_nih_reporter_search (RePORTER v2 grants).
examples: Pull recent PubMed citations on apixaban dosing in AKI.
Match this NSCLC patient to open ClinicalTrials.gov studies.
Drug pricing for a 90-day supply of metformin + lisinopril.
NIH-funded studies on early-onset Alzheimer.

skills.name: Chart-intelligence (NER + NegEx + structurer)
skills.description: Three CHART-1/2/3 tools: compute_clinical_ner (rule-based + dictionary-based NER with CUI), compute_negation_temporal (Chapman 2001 NegEx + temporal scope), compute_structure_discharge_summary (free-text → DecisionCard-shaped artifact). Used to ingest non-FHIR text from legacy EHRs.
examples: Extract clinical entities from a free-text discharge summary.
Resolve negation in `no chest pain` and `history of CHF`.
Structure a free-text admission note into a DecisionCard artifact.

skills.name: Pre-arrival triage (PREADMIT-1/2/3)
skills.description: Three Phase-7.5 patient-facing triage tools that operate on plain-language symptom descriptions before any FHIR data is available: compute_symptom_red_flag_check (regex over ACEP red-flag list — chest pain w/ radiation, focal neuro deficit, thunderclap headache, anaphylaxis, suicidal intent, etc., each tagged with severity), compute_when_to_seek_care (combines red flags + duration + self-reported severity into a 7-tier care-level recommendation: self_care → telehealth → PCP-24h → PCP-7d → urgent_care → ED_now → 911), compute_symptom_followup_questions (adaptive Q&A reducing diagnostic uncertainty before the care-level decision).
examples: Patient says 'chest pain shooting into my left arm, started 30 minutes ago'.
Caregiver says 'baby has a fever of 39.5 for the second day'.
Generate adaptive follow-up questions for 'sudden severe headache, never had this before'.
What care level for 'mild headache, started 2 hours ago, 3/10 pain'?

skills.name: Pharmacogenomic DSS (PGX-1/2/3)
skills.description: Three Phase-7.2 PGx tools that consume a patient's PGx genotypes (FHIR Genomics resource) + medication list and emit CPIC-grounded dose adjustments / drug alternatives / eligibility decisions. Curated CPIC level A/B subset covering 15 pharmacogenes and ~25 high-impact drugs (codeine/tramadol/clopidogrel/voriconazole/warfarin/statins/azathioprine/5-FU/capecitabine/carbamazepine/abacavir/primaquine/rasburicase/irinotecan). Pure-deterministic — every recommendation traces to a specific (gene, phenotype, drug) row in the curated table.
examples: Adjust warfarin starting dose for a patient with CYP2C9 *1/*3 + VKORC1 -1639 G/A.
Find alternatives to clopidogrel for a CYP2C19 poor metabolizer post-PCI.
Is a CYP2D6 test justified for a patient considered for codeine + tramadol?

skills.name: Auto-coding (CODE-1/2/3/4)
skills.description: Four CODE-1/2/3/4 tools for revenue-cycle automation: compute_icd10_suggest (ICD-10-CM from chart text + chart NER), compute_cpt_suggest (CPT codes from procedure descriptions), compute_hcpcs_suggest (HCPCS Level II J-codes for specialty drug billing), compute_coding_audit (gap report — documented_not_coded / coded_not_documented / specificity_loss / duplicate). Pure-deterministic floor with optional LLM disambiguation; every suggestion cite-backed to chart line excerpts and (when supplied) FHIR resource IDs. Addresses the $30-50 B/yr US coding-error pain-point + 10-15% claim denial rate.
examples: Suggest ICD-10 codes from this discharge summary text.
Suggest CPT codes for: MRI lumbar spine, transthoracic echocardiogram.
Suggest HCPCS J-codes for adalimumab + bevacizumab specialty drugs.
Audit this billing artifact (ICD-10 [I50.9, N17.9], CPT [99232]) against the chart text.

skills.name: Patient post-discharge Q&A + caregiver hand-off (PATIENT-Q1/2/3)
skills.description: Three patient-facing tools that work downstream of a DecisionCard / discharge summary: (1) compute_discharge_qa — keyword-routed Q&A grounded on the upstream discharge artefact with A2A `multi_turn_context_id` continuity (no LLM required for the deterministic floor); (2) compute_medication_what_if — common scenario answers (miss/double dose, alcohol, grapefruit, OTC NSAID, abrupt stop, etc.) with drug-class-specific overrides for warfarin/benzodiazepines/opioids/statins/CCBs/etc.; (3) compute_caregiver_handoff — structured 5-section caregiver hand-off (summary, key warnings, daily tasks, when to call, contact info) with Flesch-Kincaid reading-level estimate. The patient-agent specialist exposes these and demonstrates A2A composition: in a workspace, a BYO patient-facing orchestrator can consult `trustedrisk-discharge` for the DecisionCard then call `trustedrisk-patient` for the patient-language layer.
examples: Answer: 'When can I go home?' grounded on the patient's DecisionCard.
What should I do if I miss a dose of warfarin?
What if I take ibuprofen with my warfarin?
Generate a caregiver hand-off for the family of a 78y CHF patient discharged home with home-health support.

skills.name: Clinical documentation drafting (SCRIBE-1/2/3/4)
skills.description: Four scribe-agent tools that take a structured FHIR Bundle (+ optional clinician narrative blocks + DecisionCard) and produce deterministic-floor + LLM-polish-optional clinical notes: (1) compute_progress_note_draft — daily inpatient progress note in SOAP format; (2) compute_discharge_summary_draft — Joint Commission-shaped 11-section discharge summary; (3) compute_consult_letter_draft — specialty consult/referral letter back to the referring clinician; (4) compute_admission_hnp_draft — admission History and Physical with chief-complaint / HPI / PMH / PSH / meds / allergies / ROS / PE / labs / A&P sections. Each tool ships a deterministic-template floor with mandatory cite-back to FHIR observation IDs; optional LLM polish (TRUSTEDRISK_SCRIBE_LLM_POLISH=1) paraphrases prose without inventing clinical facts. Addresses clinician documentation burden (#1 cited driver of burnout, Mayo Clinic 2024 survey).
examples: Draft today's progress note for the patient on bed 14B; subjective text from voice dictation.
Generate a discharge summary for a 75y CHF admission ending tomorrow, including hospital course narrative.
Compose a cardiology consult letter back to Dr. Lee for the chest-pain rule-out.
Draft the H&P for a 45y M admitted overnight with acute pancreatitis, chief complaint epigastric pain.

skills.name: Prior Authorization — evidence + letter + likelihood (PA-1/2/3/4)
skills.description: Four PA-1/2/3/4 tools that take a structured FHIR chart + a requested service (advanced imaging, specialty drug, elective procedure, etc.) + a payer (UnitedHealth, Anthem/BCBS, Aetna, Cigna, Humana, Medicare, Medicaid, generic fallback) and produce: (1) compute_pa_evidence_pack — structured cite-backable evidence bundle from FHIR Conditions + Observations + MedicationRequests + chart NER; (2) compute_pa_payer_rules_match — payer-specific PA-criteria checklist with met/unmet/partial status + gap-closure recommendations; (3) compute_pa_appeal_likelihood — Bayesian-calibrated probability of approval with CI95 (literature priors per AMA 2024 + KFF 2025); (4) compute_pa_letter_draft — 10-section PA letter with mandatory cite-backs, optional LLM polish that paraphrases prose without inventing clinical facts (TRUSTEDRISK_PA_LLM_POLISH=1). Addresses the AMA-flagged top-3 burden ($40 B/yr US administrative cost).
examples: Build a PA evidence pack for an MRI lumbar spine for a 56y patient with sciatica unresponsive to 6 weeks of conservative therapy.
Match Aetna PA criteria for adalimumab against a Crohn's patient who has failed methotrexate and azathioprine.
Estimate UnitedHealthcare approval likelihood for a CT angiography request after one prior denial.
Draft a PA appeal letter for a Humana denial of a specialty oncology drug for a stage III NSCLC patient with EGFR exon 19 deletion.

skills.name: HEDIS / CMS Stars Rating + care-gap prioritisation (STARS-1/2/3)
skills.description: Three Phase-10.1 HEDIS / CMS Medicare Stars tools that turn a per-measure cohort summary (numerator + denominator per HEDIS measure) into a payer-ready Stars-Rating + QBP forecast: (1) compute_quality_measures_aggregate — per-measure HEDIS rates with FY 2025 CMS 5/4/3-star benchmark cuts (BCS, CCS, COL, CDC-EYE, CDC-HBA1C, CBP, MPM-ACE/DIURETIC/ANTICONV, OMW, PCR, FUH, FUM, AAB, FMC, MRP, CWP, DAE, TRC, SUPD); (2) compute_stars_rating_forecast — per-domain (preventive_care + chronic_conditions) + overall Stars projection at measurement-period end + estimated Quality Bonus Payment dollars (Avalere 2024 — 4.0 Stars unlocks ~5% benchmark QBP, 4.5+ doubles); (3) compute_care_gap_priority_ranking — top-N care-gap-closure actions ranked by expected Stars / QBP lift × difficulty (easy / moderate / hard / very_hard) with measure-specific intervention recommendations. Pure-deterministic — no LLM in the floor; addresses the $4-6 B/yr CMS QBP pain-point.
examples: Aggregate HEDIS rates for FY 2025 — BCS 0.71 (1400/1968), COL 0.66 (3300/5000), CDC-HBA1C 0.22 (440/2000).
Project this MA contract's Stars rating at end-of-measurement-year + estimate the QBP impact for 50k members.
Rank the top-10 care-gap actions by expected QBP lift for a contract with 12 open HEDIS measures.

skills.name: Population health: syndromic surveillance + vaccine reminders + DP outbreak heatmap (POPHEALTH-1/2/3)
skills.description: Three Phase-10.2 population-health tools for ACO + public-health surveillance: (1) compute_syndromic_surveillance — Poisson z-score detection of presenting-complaint clusters vs a pre-supplied seasonal baseline, with severity tiers (informational / watch / alert / outbreak) following CDC NSSP / ESSENCE; (2) compute_vaccine_reminder_cohort — per-vaccine cohort builder over the ACIP 2025 schedule (FLU, PNEUMO, ZOSTER, TDAP, HPV, COVID-19, RSV, MMR, VARICELLA, MenACWY) with per-channel uptake estimates (phone 30%, postcard 18%, ehr_portal 25%, sms 22%, email 15%); (3) compute_outbreak_heatmap — DP-noised geographic × syndrome heatmap using Laplace mechanism (configurable ε, sensitivity 1) suitable for public release without re-identification risk.
examples: Detect clusters in this 7-day ED chief-complaint summary against the 5-year seasonal baseline.
Build vaccine reminder cohorts: 1240 overdue FLU, 380 overdue PNEUMO, 95 overdue ZOSTER.
Publish a DP-noised outbreak heatmap (ε = 1.0) for ILI + GI cases across 12 ZIP buckets.

skills.name: Multi-modal: ECG QT analyzer + DICOM SR ingest (MULTIMODAL-1/2)
skills.description: Two Phase-11.4 multi-modal tools — first signal/imaging surface in TrustedRisk: (1) compute_ecg_qt_analyzer — pure-signal-processing on a 12-lead ECG strip dict (R-peak, QRS-onset, T-end indices), computes mean R-R, heart rate, QT interval, QTc Bazett + Fridericia, and the AHA/ACC/HRS 2009 sex-aware classification (normal / borderline / prolonged / severe_prolonged), with QT-prolongation risk-factor mining over the history text (electrolytes, methadone, amiodarone, sotalol, citalopram, fluoroquinolones, ondansetron, haloperidol, congenital LQTS); (2) compute_dicom_sr_ingest — surfaces a DICOM Structured Report (or FHIR DiagnosticReport) into a structured DICOMSRIngestReport with modality + body part + per-finding code/severity + impressions + conclusion. Pure-deterministic — no model in the floor.
examples: Compute QT/QTc Bazett+Fridericia on this 10-second ECG strip + flag QT-prolonging meds in the history.
Ingest this radiology DICOM SR and surface the modality + critical findings.
Score QTc on a methadone-treated patient with HR 50 and identify the risk factor.

skills.name: Insurance appeals: denial parse + letter draft + escalation path (APPEALS-1/2/3)
skills.description: Three Phase-10.3 insurance-appeals tools that turn a payer denial letter into a structured appeal pipeline. Pure-deterministic floor: (1) compute_denial_letter_parse — regex-based parser detecting payer (UnitedHealthcare / Anthem / Aetna / Cigna / Humana / Medicare / Medicaid / generic), claim id, deadlines, contested dollar amount, partial-denial flag, and per-reason category (medical_necessity / step_therapy_not_met / out_of_network / experimental_unproven / missing_documentation / duplicate_service / non_covered_benefit / claim_filing_limit / other); (2) compute_appeal_letter_draft — 8-section template (header / patient summary / denial summary / medical-necessity argument / supporting evidence / policy counter-argument / alternative proposed / closing) with mandatory cite-backs to FHIR resource ids or PubMed PMIDs, optional LLM polish flag (no model call inside the floor); (3) compute_appeal_escalation_path — payer-specific deadline + success-probability path through internal_first_level → internal_second_level → external_independent_review → state_insurance_commissioner using ERISA + ACA + KFF 2024 priors. Addresses the 10-15% US claim-denial rate.
examples: Parse this UnitedHealthcare denial letter and detect the appeal deadline + denial categories.
Draft a first-level internal appeal letter for the parsed Aetna denial citing the patient's prior step-therapy failure.
Project the full escalation path for an Anthem denial starting at internal_first_level.

extensions.description: A2A v1 FHIR-context extension. The platform delivers FHIR credentials in `Message.metadata` keyed by this URI, with camelCase fields {fhirUrl, fhirToken, patientId, fhirRefreshToken?, fhirRefreshTokenUrl?}. TrustedRisk consumes the metadata in its before-model hook, populates the shared FHIRContext ContextVar, and never lets the credentials reach the LLM prompt. See https://docs.promptopinion.ai/fhir-context/a2a-fhir-context.html.

selfCritique.description: Every clinical recommendation passes through a 4-critic ensemble (clinical_safety + fairness + evidence + llm_judge) that may downgrade confidence, force abstain, or request a replay before the response is emitted. The LLM critic has a deterministic floor (pass-through approval) so it never blocks unilaterally.

memoryLayer.description: Prior DecisionCards for the same patient are retrieved from a SQLite-backed memory store. When a valid (non-expired, same-model-version) card is found, it can serve directly; otherwise a fresh tool chain runs and detect_recommendation_drift flags any meaningful change vs the prior.

temporalValidity.description: Every RiskEstimate carries a valid_until timestamp scaled by clinical-risk severity (high LACE → 4h, moderate → 12h, low → 24h). Expired cards force a re-call.

fairnessAuditCalibration.description: Subgroup-multiplier baseline is calibrated on the receiving cohort (internal calibration workflow output) and falls back to literature defaults (HRRP/HCUP/JAMA) when the calibrated artifact is absent.

counterfactualExplanation.description: Per-factor what-if sweep shows how each LACE component contributes to the predicted risk and identifies a minimum-modification path that would flip the recommendation tier.

multiTenant.description: Optional OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant (RFC 6749 §4.4) with per-client allowed_fhir_servers allowlist enforces tenant isolation: a token issued for tenant A cannot be used to query tenant B's FHIR endpoint.

auditTrail.description: Append-only HIPAA-style audit log (PHI-redacted SHA-256 hashing) plus an RFC 6962 Merkle audit chain for tamper-evidence; reproducibility archive enables byte-identical replay of any historical decision.

rightToExplanation.description: GDPR Art. 22 / EU AI Act Art. 13 right-to-explanation surface — every DecisionCard is paired with a patient-friendly audit summary on demand.

differentialPrivacyEquity.description: Equity dashboard publishes subgroup intervention / abstain / risk rates with Laplace-mechanism differential privacy.

oauth2SecurityScheme.description: Optional bearer-token authentication (RFC 6749 §4.4). Disabled by default; enable via TRUSTEDRISK_OAUTH_ENABLED=1.

apiKeySecurityScheme.description: Static API-key authentication for marketplace-mediated A2A calls. Configured via TRUSTEDRISK_API_KEYS env var (comma-separated). When set, every A2A call must carry `X-API-Key` matching one of the configured values.
apiKeySecurityScheme.name: X-API-Key
